entry.title: Claude Context Pollution Is Real — This Is How I Solved It
entry.summary:
I keep a repo of markdown files that I use as context for Claude. Notes about how I write, project details, decisions I've made and why, things I want Claude to know about me so I don't have to re-explain them every session. Claude Code looks for a CLAUDE.md file at the root of your repo and loads it automatically. You can also pass a --system-prompt-file flag at invocation time, which lets you supply an arbitrary file as the system prompt for that session. Each markdown file in my contexts/ folder has a small frontmatter block: --- context: job-hunting title: Active Applications ---
Some files are tagged global - writing preferences, general notes about how I think. Those always get included. Everything else is opt-in by tag. ctx job-hunting # global + job-hunting files ctx essay-th…

entry.title: FastAPI vs. Django: Choosing the Best Python Framework for Your Application Needs
entry.summary:
Introduction: The Evolving Python Web Development Landscape
Python’s web development ecosystem is at a crossroads. For over a decade, Django has reigned as the go-to framework for building full-stack applications, its "batteries included" philosophy providing everything from ORM to admin panels. But the rise of FastAPI, a modern, async-first framework, is challenging this dominance—particularly in the API-centric architectures now dominating software design. The core tension? Specialization vs. integration. FastAPI, paired with a separate frontend (e.g., React, Vue), excels in microservices and high-performance APIs.
